title.narrative: Protection-focused lifesaving WASH response for conflict-affected communities in Jebel Awlia and Um Bada, Khartoum

description.narrative: ltpgtIn response to the severe disruption of WASH services in Jebel Awlia locality, Khartoum, which has left tens of thousands of conflict-affected individuals without reliable access to safe water and sanitation, Solidarités International (SI) and its local partner Sudan Zero Waste Organization (SZWO) are implementing protection-focused urgent WASH interventions, addressing immediate lifesaving needs while rehabilitating and strengthening local water systems for long-term community resilience, adapting to the feasibility and relevance of each activity. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtFollowing the signature of the Technical Agreement in February 2026, SI was formally notified that water trucking were considered non-sustainable under federal guidelines. Consequently, a first modification request submitted in February reallocated the related budget toward the solarization of an additional water yard in Jebel Awlia locality. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtSubsequently, following coordination with the Ministry of Health, SHF, and other humanitarian actors, SI identified that the four health facilities initially targeted under Activity 1.1.10 (WASH in Health Facilities) had already been covered or planned for support by other partners. In addition, the remaining facilities requiring intervention would have needed full reconstruction works exceeding the scope and budget of the current project. As a result, Activity 1.1.10 was removed in order to avoid duplication and ensure the most efficient use of humanitarian funding.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtAt the same time, joint field visits and assessments conducted with the State Water Corporation highlighted severe gaps in access to safe drinking water in targeted areas. In response, SI proposed reallocating the budget initially dedicated to Activity 1.1.10 toward additional water infrastructure rehabilitation activities under Activity 1.1.13. While initial assessments conducted in Al Rasheed administrative unit concluded that the proposed boreholes were not technically suitable for rehabilitation due to contamination and water quality concerns, the Musab Ibn Omair borehole in Um Bada locality was subsequently assessed and identified as both technically viable and critical to addressing urgent community water needs.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtUnder Activity 1.1.13, SI will rehabilitate and solarize the Musab Ibn Omair borehole in Um Bada locality, including the removal of the currently stuck pump and associated debris, to restore sustainable access to safe water for vulnerable populations. This adjustment also expands the geographical scope of the intervention beyond Jebel Awlia locality to include Um Bada locality.lt/ligtltligtIn addition, under Activity 1.1.14, SI and SZWO will strengthen one additional Water User Committees (WUCs) in Um Bada locality, to support the sustainable management, operation, and maintenance of rehabilitated water systems through inclusive community-based structures.lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgt ltbrgtThe planned intervention has been coordinated with the WASH Cluster at state and locality levels and will complement the work of partners including CARE and Almanar. Together, SI and SZWO will reach over 55,000 individuals in Jebel Awlia and Um bada locality, addressing urgent WASH needs while laying the groundwork for sustainable, community-managed services. ltbrgtlt/pgt
